full_page.content:
Feast of the Decapitation - Martyrdom of St. John the Baptist Aug. 29th 1946
My Dear Sister Mary Dorothy:
God in His infinite wisdom and merciful power give you His peace! He will give it to you - sooner or later. He must have a purpose, how- ever, in permitting you to fall - even like the rest of us. - even like against our wills. ..... He is the Master and the Judge, to recon the depth of our guilt and of our humiliation as well as how high above our- selves in His own good time He will raise ua. Only we must have patience till He change His attitude: because God is always figuring on our best. "God condescends to use our powers - if we don't spoil His plans by ours." And all this even though we be stupid sinners. For that we all are, though the whole world proclaim us heros and saints.
But why dear Sister be so anxious about tomorrow? The morrow like yesterday is in God's keeping. To worry about the past or the future is really to no purpose. Quite a different thing is to regret our blunders - and God knows we have all made plenty of them - and humbly deplore them. But worry and fret? No. Because that hell wants us to do. Rather draw good out of them by praising God for His mercy to us and His infinite patience in not kicking to blases as good for nothings .... Dear Sister Mary Dorothy: I have not been forgetting you I've had your letter of June 29 here on the desk before me ever since. I've wanted to write something worth while but am always falling be- hind with my work. To-day on coming to yours of the 14th I started this just to assure you I'd write soon. You have no idea how much I need prayers - conversion as well as u.
..... Fr. Solanus .. .... Sinner.
